summary: This article explains how growth plates near the ends of bones build new bone, how growth hormone from a small brain gland drives this, and how sleep, nutrition, and genes all shape how a child grows.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Growing Taller: How Kids' Bodies Grow” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a chemical made in the body that carries a message to tell it to do something
a body part that makes and releases a substance the body uses
something in food that the body needs to work and grow well

challengeTerms.def: describing a small gland at the base of the brain that releases growth hormone and other hormones
the process by which soft tissue, such as cartilage, hardens into bone
passed down from parents to their children through genes

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that sleep matters just as much as food for growing taller? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how growth hormone, sleep, and nutrition work together to help a child grow.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review hormone, gland, and nutrient, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses pituitary, ossification, and hereditary to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
